name: defect-fix
description: Full defect analysis and fix workflow ? analyze, diagnose, validate with failing tests, fix in small iterations.

jobs.prompt:
Triage the work. Two entry paths:

1. A GitHub board item was provided or is implied: pull it from the project's default board.
2. The user gave qualitative text describing a defect: first run /backlog to create the item on the board, then treat the newly created item as the ticket.

Immediately decide: is this a defect? Do not do any further work before making this call.

- NOT a defect (feature, improvement, or unclear): tell the parent you cannot continue and stop. Do not run start-ticket. Do not analyze.
- IS a defect: run /start-ticket immediately to create the branch and session before doing anything else. Do not bind or rely on a durable CliAgent work session on main before start-ticket — a leftover ``default`` (or folder-slug) session is the wrong bind. After start-ticket completes, rebind workspace root to the ticket worktree (``rebind_to_worktree``) on ``session/<ticket>``. The same session==branch==worktree isolation and post-start-ticket rebind must hold for CliAgent, SubAgent, and no-agent flows — not only CLI spawn. Then stop this job — analysis is next.

The ticket is confirmed as a defect and start-ticket has already been run. Now analyze:
- Read all context files (.context/, module-context.md, grill-answers).
- Analyze repo history for the area in question.
- Search for similar past incidents and related issues.
- Be thorough — do not stop at the surface.

Add your full analysis to the ticket notes under ## Analysis (separated from existing content).
jobs.judge_criteria: PASS only when: (1) context was read in full; (2) repo history and similar incidents were explored; (3) analysis was added to the ticket notes under ## Analysis.

jobs.prompt:
Diagnose the root cause of the defect. Go beyond symptoms — identify the exact underlying issue. If the root cause is unclear or ambiguous, use the /diagnose tool.

Critical distinction — make this explicit in your diagnosis:
- PROMPT/AI CHANGE: the defect is caused by incorrect, missing, or poorly structured instructions, prompts, or agent behaviour. The fix will be a change to a prompt, docstring, rule, or agent instruction — not production code.
- CODE CHANGE: the defect is caused by a bug in production code. The fix will be a code edit.
- BOTH: some defects have both a code failure and an AI/prompt failure layered on top.

State clearly which category applies. This determines what kind of tests are written next.

Before describing any product fix: announce on the ticket itself (issue comment or notes body — durable GitHub data, not only local session files) what tests are required to catch this error. Do this under ## Required tests (or equivalent on-ticket section). Cover both perspectives:
- Vanilla (mechanical) BDD: existing tests that should have caught it and why they are weak/wrong, and/or new mechanical BDD tests that are required.
- Agent BDD: existing agentic tests that should have caught it and why they are weak/wrong, and/or new agentic BDD tests that are required.
Omit a perspective only when the category clearly makes it N/A (e.g. pure prompt/AI with no mechanical side-effect may omit new mechanical BDD, but still say so explicitly). This announcement is the primary home for "what tests are required" — do it during diagnose, not during fix or as part of analysis-as-product-fix.

Add your diagnosis hypothesis, category, and required-tests announcement to the ticket notes under ## Diagnosis (and ## Required tests), separated from the analysis above.
jobs.judge_criteria: PASS only when: (1) a concrete root cause hypothesis is stated; (2) the /diagnose tool was used if the cause was not obvious; (3) the category (prompt/AI change vs code change vs both) is explicitly stated; (4) the hypothesis and category are in the ticket notes under ## Diagnosis; (5) the ticket itself announces what tests are required to catch this error (existing weak/wrong and/or new), covering both vanilla BDD and agent BDD perspectives (or explicitly N/A per category), under ## Required tests or equivalent on-ticket durable content — not only local session files.

jobs.prompt:
Write failing tests before writing any fix. Read the ## Diagnosis in the ticket to determine which tests are required:

- PROMPT/AI CHANGE: write an agentic BDD test using /agent-bdd.development. This is the primary test type for prompt or instruction defects. A mechanical BDD test is rarely needed here — but not never; include one if the prompt change also has a verifiable mechanical side-effect.
- CODE CHANGE: write a mechanical (vanilla) BDD test using /bdd.development. Also write an agentic BDD test if the code defect was causing AI/agent misbehaviour.
- BOTH: write both. Mechanical BDD first.

The listed items are context tools, not actions. Doer action is generate. Judge action is validate against what the doer generated.

The failing test is a hard requirement — write it first, run it, confirm it fails. You may alter existing tests or add new ones, but an explicit red test capturing the defect must exist before any fix is written.
jobs.judge_criteria: The judge has the same listed tools. Doer used generate; judge uses validate against what was generated. PASS only when: (1) at least one failing test exists that captures the defect; (2) for code changes: a mechanical BDD test is present; (3) for prompt/AI changes: an agentic BDD test is present; (4) mechanical BDD runs first when both are present; (5) the judge ran validate against those generated tests with those tools. Pre-existing, unrelated test failures are out of scope — do not fail the job because of failures that existed before this defect was introduced.

jobs.prompt:
Fix the defect using CleanEngineering generate at code fidelity (/clean_engineering.code) in small iterations. The listed items are context tools, not actions. Doer action is generate. Judge action is validate against what the doer generated. Work one small piece at a time ? fix just enough to make one or a few tests pass, then move to the next piece. Repeat until all BDD and agentic BDD tests are green. Run vanilla BDD first when you have both.
Before writing any code: - Explore all impacted codebases and the code they depend on. - Read module-context.md for every module you touch. - Study the existing idioms, patterns, and usage in detail. Do not invent new patterns or paradigms ? follow what is already there. A defect fix should not require new patterns.
Announce on the ticket itself (issue comment or notes body — durable GitHub data, not only local session files) under ## Weak tests and ## Fix: (1) which tests were weak or missing and what they failed to prove; (2) what you had to fix (prompt vs code vs both, files/behaviors). Do this whenever you are fixing a defect so it is trackable later. Update these sections as the fix evolves; they must be present before finish-ticket.
When this item's defect-fix jobs are complete: call finish-ticket before next_backlog_item. CliAgent backlog items use theme:cli-agent; triage the entire backlog up front before jobs.
jobs.judge_criteria: The judge has the same listed tools. Doer used generate; judge uses validate against what was generated. PASS only when: (1) all tests written for this defect pass; (2) all agentic BDD tests written for this defect pass; (3) the fix follows existing patterns, paradigms, and usage — no new patterns invented without strong justification; (4) the ticket itself documents ## Weak tests (what was weak/missing and what it failed to prove) and ## Fix (what changed); (5) the judge ran validate against the generated code and tests with those tools. Pre-existing, unrelated test failures are out of scope — judge only the tests introduced or changed for this defect, not the full suite baseline.
